findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header configured
findings.description: next.config.ts defines no headers() block, so every page is served without a Content-Security-Policy. Any script injection in the portal would run with full access to the patient session.

findings.cweName: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
findings.title: No rate limit on the one-time passcode endpoint
findings.description: The endpoint that verifies six-digit SMS passcodes has no attempt limit or throttling. An attacker can keep guessing codes for a patient's phone number until one is accepted.

findings.cweName: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
findings.title: Patient identifiers written to application logs
findings.description: The request logger serializes full request bodies, including patient names, dates of birth and insurance member ids, into logs shipped to a third-party log service. This puts PHI outside the HIPAA boundary.

findings.cweName: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
findings.title: Unrestricted file type on insurance document upload
findings.description: Uploaded insurance documents are stored under their original filename and content type without validating either. HTML and SVG files are later served from the portal's own origin, so an uploaded file can run script in other users' sessions.

findings.title: Sessions never expire server-side
findings.description: Session records have no expiry and are not revoked when a patient changes their password, so a stolen session stays valid indefinitely.
